categoryName: 大模型训练物理与涌现规律

papers.abstractEn: How efficiently can transformers store factual knowledge? The answer to this question has implications for both model design and understanding the limits of transformer-based systems. Prior studies observe a linear relationship between the number of facts memorized and the number of model parameters required, substantially worse than what theoretical analyses predict is achievable. We re-examine empirical scaling: through rigorous and systematic experiments, including extensive hyperparameter search via Bayesian optimization, we determine the smallest model that can perfectly memorize a given set of facts, and measure how this minimum size scales with the number of facts. On synthetic datasets of random, independent (subject, relation, object) triples---e.g., (Paris, capital_of, France) ---drawn at random with no exploitable structure, we find that memorization capacity, the size of the largest dataset that a model memorizes completely, grows exponentially with the transformer dimension. Equivalently, the minimum transformer dimension $d_{\min}$ required to memorize $N$ facts grows logarithmically in $N$. Across 11 dataset sizes spanning $N = 45$ to $49{,}920$, a lack-of-fit F-test does not reject the logarithmic fit (with an offset), but it does reject all other tested alternatives including power-law. Along the depth axis, however, at fixed width, the maximum memorizable dataset size grows sublinearly with the number of layers over the measured range. We further extend our exploration to structured data containing symmetric relations or two-hop composition. In this setting, we find that transformers exploit these regularities to further improve capacity. All code to reproduce our results is available at https://github.com/Magronox/transformer_information_capacity.

classification.tldr: 该研究通过系统性实验测度Transformer的事实记忆容量，发现容量随模型宽度指数增长、所需最小维度随事实数对数增长，且模型可利用结构化规律进一步提升容量。

papers.title: How Much Information Can We Fit inside a Transformer?

papers.abstractEn: Estimating neural scaling laws involves an end-to-end pipeline: designing a scaling recipe, training models across scales, evaluating models on a target metric, and deploying an algorithm to fit a scaling law to the resulting data. This final fitting stage is often treated as routine: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss using local optimization from a grid of initializations, and return the best solution found. Yet such heuristic searches can fail in two distinct ways: they offer no guarantee of returning a nearly optimal solution, and they obscure whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. Indeed, we show that standard scaling law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect (Breiman, 2001): the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. We resolve these issues with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and exhaustively maps the near-minimizers to the implied range of scaling curves.

classification.tldr: 该文揭示缩放律拟合中的Rashomon效应：近似最优参数区域可导致大相径庭的外推，并提出分支定界算法保证近优拟合并穷举所有近优解。

papers.title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation

papers.abstractEn: Broad classes of deep generative models (DGMs) operate by learning to map a simple source distribution, such as a standard Gaussian, to a complex high-dimensional target distribution. Despite their success, DGMs often empirically struggle to accurately represent distributions with heavy tails or well-separated modes. In this work, we show that these difficulties reflect intrinsic properties of the underlying transport problem rather than particular neural network architectures or training procedures. We establish quantitative lower bounds on the gradients and Jacobians of pushforward mappings that transport log-concave source distributions to such targets. For heavy-tailed target distributions, the required gradient magnitude grows as the target develops increasingly large moments. For multimodal target distributions, the low-probability regions between well-separated modes similarly force large gradients in the transport map. We discuss how such large derivatives relate to trade-offs between expressivity and numerical stability. Our results hold under substantially weaker regularity conditions than previous analyses and remain stable under perturbations of the target distribution. Finally, we show that these obstructions can be mitigated when the goal is approximation of a given density rather than generative modeling. Specifically, we propose simple classes of bijective reparametrizations that can alleviate the difficult geometric structure and reduce the gradient burden placed on the learned generative map. Numerical experiments support our theoretical analysis.

classification.tldr: 从最优传输角度证明推前式生成模型在重尾和多峰目标分布上存在内在梯度障碍，并提出双射重参数化方法缓解该几何困难。

papers.title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models

papers.abstractEn: In this work, generalization in machine learning is investigated using a predator-prey model. We overview biological and chemical interpretation of the stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics and generative adversarial network. For a particular example of recovering an unknown function by a polynomial of fixed degree from a set of noisy data, the predator-prey model provides better approximation compared to the gradient descent method. Further, thermodynamical arguments, in particular Eyring formula, are used to explain grokking (delayed generalization) phenomenon in machine learning.

classification.tldr: 该工作用捕食者-猎物模型和热力学论证（Eyring公式）从理论上解释机器学习中的泛化与grokking延迟泛化现象，并在多项式函数恢复任务上验证其近似优于梯度下降。

papers.title: Generalization in Learning: Eyring Formula and Predator-prey Model

papers.abstractEn: Muon has achieved strong empirical performance in large-scale language-model training, motivating a better theoretical understanding of its practical implementation. Unlike the idealized polar-factor update, practical Muon uses a fixed number of quintic Newton--Schulz iterations. Existing analyses mainly establish average- or best-iterate stationarity guarantees, leaving last-iterate convergence less understood. We study last-iterate gradient convergence of practical finite-step Muon on smooth, lower-bounded nonconvex objectives. For deterministic gradients, we show that without input stabilization, Muon can cycle even on a smooth convex quadratic. With positive stabilization, we establish last-iterate gradient convergence for any fixed momentum coefficient below one and a sufficiently small constant learning rate, together with square-summability of gradients. For stochastic gradients, we first show that persistent bounded, unbiased noise can prevent convergence with fixed learning rates and momentum, even with positive stabilization. We then establish almost-sure and mean-square last-iterate gradient convergence by combining decreasing learning rates with increasing momentum under bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Finally, we construct a smooth counterexample showing that neither convergence theorem guarantees a pointwise polynomial rate. We further establish density-one convergence rates, guaranteeing polynomial gradient decay for all but a vanishing fraction of iterations.

classification.tldr: 对实用有限步Newton-Schulz迭代的Muon优化器建立末次迭代梯度收敛理论，并给出发散与反例分析。

papers.title: Last-Iterate Stationarity of Muon with Finitely Many Newton-Schulz Iterations

papers.abstractEn: Entropy in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) moves up or down depending on choices that should be neutral, such as whether over-length responses are masked or counted as failures. We trace this to sampler mismatch, where rollouts are drawn with top-k/top-p truncation or at a temperature the learner does not apply, and prove that a constant advantage shift then changes the entropy of a softmax policy, at first order and in expectation, with a sign fixed by the sampler: positive shifts sharpen the policy under any sampler whose likelihood ratio to the policy increases with token probability, including top-k, top-p, min-p, and temperatures below one, and flatten it under flatter samplers. In group-based RLVR with token-level losses, the baseline-controlled part of this drift is set by the token-weighted net advantage, which masking and failing over-length responses can push to opposite signs; the remainder, a covariance between advantages and the sampler's sharpness gap, can feed back over long horizons. On a 2B model, the entropy slope is linear in shifts of the net advantage under truncated sampling and indistinguishable from flat under exact sampling, and token-level importance ratios leave 98% of the drift. In 100-step runs, a net-zero baseline only delays an entropy explosion that exact sampling does not show, a fixed positive shift delays it further, and a baseline weighted by the sharpness gap keeps entropy stable without changing the learner. On a 9B reasoning model over ten steps, the uncorrected rule loses held-out accuracy, whereas zeroing the net advantage or renormalizing the learner gains 8.2 and 8.8 points over it, with no held-out effect under exact sampling.

classification.tldr: 分析了RLVR中采样器失配导致的熵漂移规律，证明其符号由采样器决定，并提出基于净优势归零或重整化的熵稳定修正，提升推理模型准确率。

papers.title: A Sign Law for Entropy Drift under Sampler Mismatch in RLVR

papers.abstractEn: The differential neural tangent kernel (DNTK) is a tool for analyzing the training dynamics of overparameterized physics informed neural networks. In this work, we investigate the symmetry of the infinite DNTK under an orthogonal group, for two layer and deep neural networks separately, based on the explicit expression of the DNTK and recursive formula, respectively. The results are for all activations with or without a bias term, and shed insight into the structure of the infinite width DNTK. Then we prove that the integral operators over the unit sphere induced by operators from the same group orbit share the spectrum, and their reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces differ only by an orthogonal transformation, and that the operator fixed DNTK exhibits zonal symmetry on the unit sphere for symmetric operators. Thus the eigenvalue decay rate of the associated integral operator can be derived for shallow networks with RePU activation and zero bias initialization.

classification.tldr: 该文从理论上证明无限宽度微分神经正切核在正交群下的对称性，并由此导出RePU激活浅层网络积分算子的特征值衰减率。

papers.title: The Symmetry of Differential Neural Tangent Kernel under the Orthogonal Group

papers.abstractEn: Most analyses of neural representations focus on trained endpoints, leaving the process by which internal structure forms comparatively unmeasured. We instead treat representation formation itself as an object of study, asking whether the path a representation takes through training reveals information that its endpoint does not. We formalize this idea by viewing representation learning as a geometric trajectory, using Bures geometry to measure movement through representation space and quantum Fisher information to characterize local sensitivity to input factors. We find that learning concentrates local sensitivity on task-relevant factors, and that changing only the prediction target reorganizes this geometry around the corresponding visual factor. More strikingly, representation trajectories become systematically less direct as the learned computation requires higher-order interactions among input factors. This effect persists under matched-performance and training-duration controls and transfers from synthetic vector inputs to residual CNNs on rendered and natural images. Importantly, formation history contains predictive information about the stability of the learned representation: controlling for interaction order, path tortuosity predicts its subsequent drift under continued training and sensitivity to parameter perturbations, whereas endpoint displacement does not. Finally, representation-aware optimization lets us actively shape these trajectories, showing that formation geometry is not only measurable but actionable. Together, these results establish representation formation as a new source of information about learning: its geometry reveals properties of the computation being constructed, predicts subsequent representational stability, and provides a target for intervention during optimization.

classification.tldr: 该文用Bures几何和量子Fisher信息刻画训练中表征形成的轨迹，发现路径几何能预测表征稳定性并可主动干预优化过程。

papers.title: The Information Geometry of Representation Formation

papers.abstractEn: Early stopping is commonly used to prevent fitting label noise from degrading generalization. Does this mean that, when a positive fraction of the training labels is intrinsically unpredictable, the best test error must occur before interpolation? Experiments on a CIFAR10 classification task with randomly labeled examples motivate the opposite possibility: although fixed-feature and shallow models exhibit late-time deterioration of the test error, the need for early stopping essentially disappears in larger, deeper convolutional networks even after the random labels have all been classified correctly. We determine when late-time deterioration disappears entirely in a solvable setting. For kernel gradient flow on a synthetic noisy classification task, we derive sharp high-dimensional learning curves and obtain a phase diagram controlled by the balance between the linear kernel component that learns the shared relation between inputs and labels and the higher-order components that enable fitting the label noise. In one regime, generalization is optimized at finite time and early stopping is necessary. In another, generalization improves until interpolation, but the endpoint is suboptimal across kernels. At the boundary, the interpolating endpoint attains the lowest generalization error across the considered kernel family and all training times. Thus, even with extensive irreducible label noise, interpolation can outperform early stopping. The neural-network experiments leave open how learned representations acquire an analogous favorable geometry.

classification.tldr: 该论文通过核梯度流的高维学习曲线推导出标签噪声下早停收益的相图，揭示了核线性分量与高阶分量的平衡决定早停必要、插值最优或二者等价三种机制。

papers.title: When is early stopping beneficial under label noise? A phase diagram for kernel gradient flow

papers.abstractEn: Deep learning models tend to perform best at large widths and depths. The growing interest in scaling laws, especially in the language modeling domain, has motivated procedures for scaling up network widths and depths in order to preserve stability and computational efficiency of training dynamics. Existing depth-scaling approaches force a choice between retaining locally maximal \emph{feature learning} and preserving a form of \emph{feature diversity} in the residual stream arising from random differences between channels. We examine a \textit{joint scaling recipe} that preserves both. With residual width $N_\flat$, hidden width $N_\sharp$, and depth $L$, the key quantity is, by default, the limiting ratio $N_\flat/(N_\sharp L)\toα$, while correlated initialization (Half Copy) can partially relax the resulting shape constraints. Theory and residual-MLP experiments support convergence at fixed positive $α$ to an SDE limit with locally maximal feature learning. Hidden computations can then be redistributed between width and depth while preserving this limit, like turning melody into harmony and back. Language-model experiments nevertheless show performance differences under regrouping at fixed parameter count. These results distinguish approximating a limit (ODE or SDE) from scaling for better performance.

classification.tldr: 提出一种联合缩放残差结构的方案，在深度缩放时同时保持特征学习与特征多样性，并以SDE极限理论支撑其实验结果。

papers.title: Sliding Networks: A Family of Residual Structures Preserving Feature Learning and Feature Diversity

papers.abstractEn: We study the geometry and closure of spaces of functions realized by ReLU neural networks of fixed architecture. We first establish a general result about limits of continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) functions: the minimum number of convex sets on which a function is affine is lower semicontinuous under pointwise convergence. The proof uses a connection to hypergraph coloring and a compactness principle, and yields quantitative bounds on the polyhedral complexity of continuous limits. We then characterize the functions realizable by shallow ReLU networks with vector-valued outputs, extending a known scalar-valued characterization. Using this and the geometry of limiting hyperplane arrangements, we prove that fixed-width shallow scalar ReLU realization spaces are closed in the weighted supremum norm on the whole input space. In contrast, we construct an explicit sequence of networks with architecture $(2,3,2\mid1)$ whose limit is not realizable by that architecture. Non-closedness holds both globally in weighted supremum norm and under uniform convergence on compact sets with nonempty interior, disproving a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan, and Voigtlaender. Finally, we show that non-closedness for a fixed scalar-output ReLU architecture necessarily involves a \emph{blow-up residue}, in which diverging output coefficients amplify an emerging linear dependence among hidden features. Together, these results provide geometric and functional-analytic tools for studying the boundaries and degenerations of ReLU realization spaces.

classification.tldr: 该论文用几何与泛函分析工具研究固定架构ReLU网络实现空间的极限结构，证明某些浅层网络实现空间非闭，并刻画了非闭性所需的爆炸残差机制。

papers.title: The Geometry of Limits in ReLU Function Spaces

papers.abstractEn: In this work, we propose a unified framework for training algorithms across different stages of modern large language model development, based on the perspective of distribution matching. We show that a broad class of language model training algorithms can be interpreted as minimizing a certain divergence between the current model and a target distribution, and that characterizing the properties of this target distribution provides substantial insight into the behavior of the corresponding training algorithms. By analyzing specific forms of the target distribution, we establish that On-Policy Distillation (OPD) enjoys an advantage over classical Knowledge Distillation (KD) when the current model distribution is close to the target distribution, while exhibiting a disadvantage when the two distributions are far apart. Furthermore, when the target distribution itself depends on the model being optimized, we show that the accumulation of estimation variance can induce a deterministic degradation of the target distribution. These results provide a theoretical explanation, at least in part, for the long-term behavior of existing Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms. With this intuition we further designed Conditional KL (CKL) regularization for mitigating the degradation of the target distribution. CKL can effectively preserve mode diversity while relaxing the constraint imposed by classical KL regularization on reward improvements. We believe this theoretical perspective can bring some new understanding of language model training algorithms and provide useful guidance for future research.

classification.tldr: 以分布匹配视角统一解释各类大模型训练算法，理论分析在线蒸馏与经典知识蒸馏的适用条件、RL目标分布退化的成因，并提出条件KL正则以缓解该退化并保留模式多样性。

papers.title: A Distribution-Matching Perspective on LLM Training Algorithms

papers.abstractEn: We prove identifiability results for constant-width residual networks with polynomial activations and bias terms. For activations of degree at least five with generic coefficients, the fiber over a generic parameter is a singleton. For activations of degree at least three with no linear term after a suitable translation of the input, the generic fiber is given by translating biases and then scaling weights and translated biases by real roots of unity. These results specialize to networks without bias terms. With the same proof technique, we further derive necessary conditions for critical points of the ResNet parametrization, that are central in singular learning theory.

classification.tldr: 从理论上证明多项式激活残差网络在一般意义下的参数可辨识性，并据此推导出ResNet参数化临界点的必要条件。

papers.title: Polynomial Residual Networks are Generically Identifiable

papers.abstractEn: The discovery of scaling laws enables prediction of the performance, the optimal resource allocation strategy, and the best hyperparameter configuration of a large-scale training job based on inexpensive experiments at smaller scales. Guided by these empirical scaling laws, the deep learning community has achieved great success in training large (self-)supervised models on Internet-scale datasets. In contrast, despite its potential and wide application, reinforcement learning (RL) has yet to find a guiding principle for predictable scaling. In this work, we conduct an empirical study of RL scaling laws of an actor-critic algorithm in two procedurally generated environments, Starpilot and Craftax. We discover empirical scaling laws with strong predictive performance in both environments. The discovered scaling laws accurately predict the aforementioned three quantities for larger-scale training jobs up to two orders of magnitude in total training compute. In particular, we employ a variant of Elo scores for the single-agent RL paradigm as an alternative performance metric than the commonly used mean episode return. Our results show that the Elo score is a much more predictable metric than the mean episode return, making it a better choice for fitting scaling laws. By applying our discovered scaling laws to increase training compute, we establish a new state of the art in the challenging Craftax environment. Beneath the surface of the global scaling trend, we also observe a non-monotonic scaling pattern of the compute-optimal model size in Craftax. We connect this observation to a pathology known as Ray interference.

classification.tldr: 通过在两个程序化环境中进行实证研究，发现了强化学习训练的缩放规律，可预测大规模训练的性能与最优资源配置，并提出Elo分数作为更可预测的性能指标。

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning Scaling Laws

papers.abstractEn: Training is often stopped at a data-dependent time, as in early stopping, and the last iterate is kept. Guarantees valid at such times must hold at all times simultaneously. We determine the optimal time-uniform rate for the last iterate of clipped SGD on smooth convex objectives under heavy-tailed noise with a bounded central $p$th moment, $1<p\le2$. A schedule without horizon or confidence inputs attains $\tilde O(t^{-β_p})$ at all times, with $β_p=2(p-1)/(3p-1)$, also almost surely, and no rule that steps along the stochastic gradient at its current iterate attains $\tilde O(t^{-r})$ for any $r>β_p$, even with adaptive step sizes and thresholds. This rate lies between the optimal rate $O(T^{-α_p})$ for a known horizon $T$, $α_p=(p-1)/p$, and the previous time-uniform rate $\tilde O(t^{-2(p-1)/(3p)})$ (Chezhegov et al., ICLR 2026); under finite variance, the exponents are $1/2$, $2/5$, and $1/3$. Their conjecture that a better schedule reaches the optimal rate thus holds with a known horizon, as shown by Liu and by Jiang et al., but fails without one. Querying gradients at the running average of the iterates attains $\tilde O(t^{-α_p})$ at all times, whereas heavy-ball momentum with geometric forgetting and polynomially bounded steps cannot improve on $β_p$.

classification.tldr: 该文研究重尾噪声下裁剪SGD在未知时域停止时最后迭代的收敛率，证明时间一致最优率为O~(t^{-β_p})，并说明已知时域才能达到最优率，从而否定此前关于更优调度的猜想。

papers.title: The Cost of an Unknown Horizon for the Last Iterate of Clipped SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise

papers.abstractEn: Diffusion models trained on increasingly large datasets sampled from the same data distribution will converge to the same learned distribution. However, in practice, a model trained on finite data depends on the particular training dataset; this dependence is reflected in properties of the model's outputs, such as memorization and sample quality. To understand this dependence through an information-theoretic lens, we study \textit{model information}, a computationally tractable measure of how much samples from the trained model depend on the particular training dataset. We explore its scaling behavior as model size and training dataset size vary. Specifically, we uncover two qualitatively distinct scaling regimes: (1) a nonlinear model information regime marking the transition from pure memorization to imperfect generalization, and (2) a generalization regime characterized by linear scaling of the model information and progressively improved generalization and sample quality. We then posit an information-theoretically principled scaling law to quantify these two regimes, and show that this law yields induced scaling laws for memorization and sample quality. We finally demonstrate that these induced scaling laws extrapolate well outside the fit's domain. Our results demonstrate information-theoretic principles for memorization and sample quality scaling laws in diffusion models. Our code is publicly available on \href{https://github.com/DruvPai/diffusion_info_theory_scaling_law}{GitHub}.

classification.tldr: 论文从信息论视角研究扩散模型随模型与数据规模变化的记忆化与样本质量规律，提出可外推的信息论缩放定律并划分出两个不同的缩放区间。

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Scaling Laws for Generative Diffusion Training

papers.abstractEn: Deep learning architectures tend to generalize well to unseen data, but explaining this capability is still an open area of research. Under the assumption of i.i.d. data, PAC-Bayes provides a bound on generalization error, and its tightness relies on a parameter distribution that covers a large volume of low-loss solutions. The Fisher information metric endows the parameter space with a geometry for which distances reflect functional changes, and whose zero-component captures functional invariances. We define and study a Fisher-aligned parameter distribution for which we can simultaneously guarantee (1) a low-loss, thanks to the exploration constrained on the functional invariances and (2) a large log-volume of parameters, proportional to the number of zero eigenvalues. This distribution results in a high-probability generalization error bound, which scales with the expected rank of the Fisher information matrix, shedding light on the relevance of this quantity.

classification.tldr: 构造Fisher对齐的参数分布并证明其期望Fisher秩越低则PAC-Bayes泛化界越紧，从理论上解释深度网络的良好泛化能力。

papers.title: Lower expected Fisher rank implies better PAC generalization

papers.abstractEn: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is now a standard approach to parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks. Its low-rank factorization is inherently non-identifiable, making LoRA a singular statistical model whose learning complexity cannot be described by parameter dimension alone. We study this complexity using the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) from singular learning theory and how it depends on both the low-rank parameterization and the pretrained network. Under a local linearization, LoRA induces a low-rank trace regression model whose Kullback--Leibler geometry is controlled by a forward-backward covariance, constructed from activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer. This covariance determines which low-rank perturbations are statistically observable. When it is nondegenerate along the relevant low-rank directions, we recover the classical learning complexity of reduced-rank regression; when its kernel meets these directions, additional statistically indistinguishable parameters change the singular geometry. We characterize this geometry locally through observable tangent directions and a residual singularity, and globally through affine linear sections of determinantal varieties. The global learning complexity need not be determined at a ground-truth parameter, as singularities on another rank stratum can dominate. We also introduce a curvature-corrected multi-temperature estimator of the RLCT. Experiments on multilayer perceptron and transformer architectures reveal strongly layer-dependent forward-backward geometry and show that ambient covariance degeneracy does not imply degeneracy along the low-rank directions relevant to adaptation.

classification.tldr: 用奇异学习理论的实对数典范阈值刻画LoRA低秩微调的统计学习复杂度，揭示其奇异几何依赖前向-反向协方差的退化结构。

papers.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.abstractEn: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.

classification.tldr: 将逐层谱特征学习方法扩展出反向耦合机制，理论上证明其能恢复前向方法无法捕捉的低层特征方向并提升训练精度。

papers.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning

papers.abstractEn: Large language models are trained to predict tokens from a finite vocabulary, each represented by a vector in a $d$-dimensional embedding space. Therefore, token prediction is a classification problem whose classes have a geometry determined by the embedding. We study how this geometry affects learning in a minimal solvable model: a linear predictor that maps a sequence of $N$ embedded tokens to a $d$-dimensional output through one $d\times d$ matrix per position, trained in the teacher--student setting. We call this the \textit{token perceptron}. We compute its generalization error with the replica method, taking $N\to\infty$ at fixed number of examples per position $α=P/N$ and keeping $d$ and the vocabulary size $D$ finite. As a first reference case, we consider continuous embeddings on the sphere, which isolate the role of the embedding dimension. The natural load is then $α/d$, and for $d>1$ a normalized label fixes the direction of the teacher output, so the problem becomes a noiseless regression: the teacher is recovered exactly above $α_{\rm rec}=d^2/(d-1)$, and spherical cross-entropy reaches this threshold at large inverse temperature. In the same setting the storage capacity of random associations scales as $d^2$ for margins $O(1/\sqrt{d})$. We then turn to vocabulary embeddings, where a label only identifies the Voronoi cell of the teacher output, so that each example imposes inequalities rather than equations, as in the classical perceptron. We compute the Bayes-optimal error for a given embedding matrix through an approximate spectral closure and show that the optimal learner first resolves the directions in which the vocabulary has the largest variance, even when the teacher is isotropic.

classification.tldr: 通过可解的token感知机模型用复本方法刻画词嵌入几何如何影响分类学习的泛化误差、恢复阈值与存储容量。

papers.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary

papers.abstractEn: Several formal theories have been developed to characterize the capabilities and limitations of the transformer architecture, each employing different abstractions that capture different features of the architecture. Due to the differences in their underlying assumptions and conceptual frameworks, these theories can disagree in their predictions about what tasks transformers find easy or hard. We map out seven theories of transformer capability (Star-free, $\mathsf{AC}^0$, $\mathsf{TC}^0$, C-RASP, MPC, BAPO, and Sensitivity) and translate their results into a common matrix of predictions across a suite of tasks covering different computational structures. We provide new theoretical results to complete this matrix. We then evaluate theoretical predictions through controlled experiments measuring in-distribution sample complexity, length generalization, and pretrained language model performance. We find that no single theory explains the observed pattern of successes and failures. When a theory does not capture the transformer behaviors relevant to a task, its predictions break down; for instance, we show that the $k$-hop induction task is predicted hard by C-RASP because it does not model content-dependent attention, but we train small transformers on this task that length-generalize. Similarly, theories assuming hard attention like $\mathsf{AC}^0$ and BAPO predict binary majority to be hard, for which we also find success in practice. Together, our results point to several specific features that a theory of transformers must capture: soft rather than hard attention, dynamic content-dependent retrieval, bounded computation at each position, an account of learnability and inductive biases, and a combination of upper and lower bounds.

classification.tldr: 该论文将七种transformer能力理论统一到同一任务预测矩阵并用实验检验，发现没有单一理论能解释实际表现，指出未来理论需刻画软注意力、内容依赖检索与可学习性等特征。

papers.title: Putting Transformer Theories to the Test

papers.abstractEn: Regularisation-based class-incremental learning (CIL) methods control the stability-plasticity trade-off through fixed coefficients tuned offline, independently of the continual learning objective and blind to phase-specific variations in data volume, task difficulty, and class similarity. We argue this is a fundamental mismatch and propose REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning, which treats regularisation strength selection as a sequential decision problem. At each incremental phase, a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) agent observes a compact state of current performance metrics and incoming data statistics, and outputs the distillation coefficients for that phase. To respect CIL's constraint on historical data access, the policy is trained entirely on pseudo-CIL tasks constructed from the initial phase, then deployed on the incremental sequence without further adaptation. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that REDAR reduces forgetting and improves forward transfer over fixed and heuristic baselines, and that policies trained on short pseudo-task horizons transfer effectively to longer incremental runs.

classification.tldr: 将类增量学习中的正则化系数选择建模为序贯决策问题，用轻量RL代理在每个增量阶段自适应输出蒸馏系数，减少遗忘并提升前向迁移。

papers.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning

papers.abstractEn: Looped language models apply one block of layers repeatedly, and the design pays off only if depth is reusable: loop steps beyond the trained budget must remain usable at inference. We ask whether that rests on normalising the state between loop steps, as the released Ouro models do, or on agreement between the loop a model is trained with and the loop it is run with. On released weights this loop-boundary normalisation can be removed without adding parameters and with the readout path bit-identical, and the operation is an identity at one loop step, which serves as an implementation check. Removing it takes Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B to zero accuracy by the trained budget on a balanced binary task (chance 0.500). State-norm growth, the failure that prior accounts predict, is not the cause: the norm stays within a factor of 2.021 while the head commits to a single wrong token. Yet in 19M-parameter models trained from scratch on two synthetic tasks, 16 seeds per configuration, training without the normalisation is never worse than training with it and extrapolates better: the two are closest at the trained depth and separate on both sides of it (Cliff's delta up to 0.867 beyond the budget). Both results follow if agreement, and not the normalisation itself, is what keeps depth reusable. The damage sits in the readout together with the last layer of the block: in the models trained from scratch, refitting the head over the frozen modified loop recovers a third of the lost accuracy and plateaus, while refitting the last block layer with it recovers all of it. Finally, comparing looped with stacked depth at an equal inference loop count is confounded by unequal overshoot of the trained budget; at matched overshoot the advantage of looping vanishes on one task and shrinks on the other.

classification.tldr: 通过实验分析循环语言模型深度可复用性的成因，发现关键在于训练与推理时循环步数的一致性而非状态归一化，并指出循环与堆叠深度的对比受预算过冲混淆。

papers.title: Agreement rather than normalisation keeps depth reusable in looped language models

papers.abstractEn: Synthetic rewrites, where a language model rewrites a natural document e.g. into a target style, are now a standard ingredient of pretraining corpora. However, critical aspects of their use remain poorly understood, such as how much compute should be spent rewriting training data and whether a model trained on rewrites can outperform the rewriter. We study these two questions by proposing a rewriting scaling law that predicts loss from model size, training tokens, the fraction of training tokens that are rewrites, and the number of epochs over the natural data, charging the compute spent generating rewrites. We fit this scaling law in two settings. In the compute-limited setting, natural data is plentiful and rewrites come from a third-party rewriter trained with more compute than our largest run. We find that the estimated optimal rewrite fraction increases with compute, from under $10\%$ at $3\times10^{18}$ FLOPs to $32\%$ at $10^{22}$ FLOPs. Our scaling forecast extrapolates $33\times$ in FLOPs to train a 22B-parameter model, whose final loss is within $1.1\%$ of our prediction. This model achieves a better BPB than its rewriter on several web domains at one-tenth the rewriter's training compute. In the data-limited setting, we assume we only have a fixed seed set of natural data and that our rewriter is a model of the same size as the target, pretrained on that seed set. Again, we find the optimal rewrite fraction increases with the compute budget. We also demonstrate that a model trained on rewrites of its own pretraining data, generated by a rewriter of the same size, beats the best run on natural data alone at every model size up to 3B. Our results show that synthetic rewriting can be studied through the scaling law lens: that optimal methodological choices are predictable and scaling does not necessarily break down beyond the rewriter's capabilities.

classification.tldr: 提出合成改写数据的缩放律，预测最优改写比例随算力增长，并证明基于改写数据训练的模型可超越改写器本身。

papers.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints

papers.abstractEn: We study the early training dynamics of nonlinear residual networks with blocks of zero hidden layers as a model of more general residual networks. We analyze networks in a sequential limit where first width and depth diverge, then the number of training data points diverges, and finally the input dimension diverges. This is a more refined setup compared to the typical mean-field theory analysis in which depth and width diverge but the number of training datapoints and input dimension are fixed. Our main technical result is a diagrammatic computation of both the network output and the hidden representations after the few steps of gradient descent in terms of the statistics of inner products of inputs from the training set. One of our principle conceptual findings is a negative result: in the limit of large input dimension the network output can learn only a linear function of its inputs early in training since higher learned monomials are more and more suppressed in the input dimension and vanish in the large dimension limit. This suggests that mean-field limits of ResNets are surprisingly rigid in the regime of high input dimension and may not be sufficient toy models for understanding feature learning. Finally, we investigate how to ensure hyperparameter transfer for the learning rate as a function of dataset size and input dimension. We test our predictions numerically and find excellent agreement with our theory.

classification.tldr: 通过图方法分析残差网络早期训练动力学，证明高维输入下早期训练只能学习线性函数，提示平均场极限不足以刻画特征学习。

papers.title: Early learning in large residual networks

papers.abstractEn: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $α>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((κ_P\log(m/δ)/m)^α)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $κ_P=(P/κ_1^*+(1-P)/κ_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-δ$. The constants $κ_0^*$ and $κ_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $α=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $κ_0^*=4\sqrt{2}τ(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $τ\ge1$, and $κ_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $τ=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.

classification.tldr: 该文从理论上刻画部分可训练网络从随机特征到全可训练网络的逼近率相变，证明少量可训练参数即可捕获大部分逼近误差下降。

papers.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks

papers.abstractEn: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously-observed "Slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.

classification.tldr: 该文发现并修复了softmax与交叉熵标准实现中的两个数值bug，消除了Slingshot现象，加速grokking并稳定蒸馏中的学生网络训练。

papers.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy

papers.abstractEn: The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.

classification.tldr: 该文提出用子空间鲁棒Wasserstein距离分析高维贝叶斯推断中ULA算法的偏差与混合时间，证明在过参数化和大样本情形下可获得与维度无关的复杂度界。

papers.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis

papers.abstractEn: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits. We first show, theoretically and empirically, that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate. This motivates us to investigate structured noise arising from mini-batch sampling in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies. We establish an exact balancing threshold for two tasks and extend the analysis to multiple tasks, revealing how task coverage and gradient reliability jointly shape learning. Our analysis shows that Muon can soften the dependence on task frequency from linear to square-root, helping balance the learning of frequent and rare tasks. We further identify rotation-induced negative transfer in SignSGD that Muon avoids, and explain how momentum reduces sampling noise while tracking changing gradients. Controlled numerical experiments validate these mechanisms, and a preliminary LLM pretraining study illustrates the practical promise of fast-slow momentum.

classification.tldr: 理论分析Muon优化器中结构化梯度噪声对预条件的作用，证明其可将任务频率依赖从线性 soften 为平方根，并解释动量减少采样噪声的机制。

papers.title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise

papers.abstractEn: Modern transformers often solve complex tasks by generating and refining intermediate reasoning steps. To develop a theoretical understanding of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, a notable recent study by Huang et al. (2025) viewed transformers as algorithm executors, and showed that when transformers' CoT steps are supervised by a gradient-descent teacher, they can learn to implement gradient descent for in-context weight prediction in linear regression. In this paper, we study the same in-context weight prediction task but ask whether CoT reasoning can go beyond merely imitating the teacher algorithm. We show that, after initial supervision from a gradient-descent teacher, further trajectory-level supervision using the true regression weights leads the model to implement the Heavy-Ball method, thereby achieving acceleration over the original teacher. Notably, this accelerated algorithm emerges without supervision from any Heavy-Ball teacher. Our results provide a concrete theoretical example in which transformer reasoning can discover new algorithms through training, rather than merely imitate the algorithm used for supervision.

classification.tldr: 理论上证明Transformer通过轨迹级监督可在梯度下降教师基础上自发涌现Heavy-Ball加速算法，说明CoT推理能发现新算法而非仅模仿教师。

papers.title: Transformers with CoT Discover Heavy-Ball Acceleration Through Training

papers.abstractEn: Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data. We trace the word through open models' training histories, reading it with label-free indices of frequency, position, form and usage and an injected-error test, all computed from sampled outputs. We find that zero-RL almost never coins the marker: on bases that lack the word, RL raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially while {wait} stays near absent. It arrives with training data: mid-training in OLMo-3, and fine-tuning on reasoning traces installs it in most models whose base lacks it. Where the base already uses it, both released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply it, whereas KL-free GRPO from the same base does not; OLMo-3's recipe wears down its form and makes it a more sensitive but more liberal alarm; RL after supervised fine-tuning barely changes it, and our GRPO recipe erases a marker seeded by fine-tuning. Finally, we show that marker frequency alone does not indicate RL-induced reasoning and caution against LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics, as automated judges can reverse human-labelled trends.

classification.tldr: 通过无标签频率、位置与用法指标追踪推理模型中wait一词的来源，发现它主要由SFT与预训练数据引入而非RL发明，RL只是放大已有标记，并警示LLM裁判指标可能逆转人工标注趋势。

papers.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models

papers.abstractEn: Synthetic pretraining under distribution shift requires deciding what synthetic data to use. A natural criterion is to match the spectral predictability $Ω$ of the source to the target, but is $Ω$ sufficient? We test this hypothesis, which we call predictability-aware pretraining, across three architectures (LSTM, PatchTST, TCN) and three seeds. Under ideal synthetic-to-synthetic conditions, $Ω$-matched pretraining can outperform even an oracle baseline (+46.8% MSE reduction, LSTM), though the benefit is already architecture-dependent. On the real-world ETTm1 benchmark, however, this relationship does not hold: sine-plus-noise pretraining at matched $Ω$ yields only a marginal mean improvement +2.3% averaged over all three architectures, up to +65.5% on individual channels), whereas $Ω$ matched chaotic ODE trajectories systematically degrade performance -13.2%). The two sources agree on the direction of transfer for only 53% of configurations across all three architectures (Pearson r=-0.02), indicating that $Ω$ carries little information about which source will transfer beneficially. We further observe an architecture-dependent asymmetry in the response to the direction of the $Ω$ gap. We conclude that $Ω$ matching can help in controlled settings but is not sufficient to predict transfer across sources, and we discuss additional signal properties that a source-selection criterion may need to consider.

classification.tldr: 实证检验以谱可预测性匹配作为合成预训练数据选择准则的有效性，发现该准则在受控合成场景有效但在真实基准上无法预测迁移收益。

papers.title: Is spectral predictability enough? Testing Ω-matching for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift

papers.abstractEn: We study generative reward models (GenRMs) as online preference providers for policy optimization in creative writing. Across Qwen3 reward-model sizes from 0.6B to 14B, Thinking judges trained with GRPO have higher static Gold-label accuracy than Answer-Only judges trained with SFT. This ranking often reverses when the judges train policies through online DPO: Answer-Only rewarders yield higher peak and top-five-average policy Elo in seven of eight matched settings under a fixed, learned 32B Gold evaluator. Intermediate Thinking-judge checkpoints can also outperform later, more statically accurate checkpoints as rewarders. Sweeps over rewarder size, policy size, training duration and DPO regularization show substantial benefits from reward-model capacity, including judges larger than the policy. We analyze trajectories with evaluator-specific Elo arenas, conditional match-resampling intervals and descriptive scaling fits. These results demonstrate an evaluator-rewarder gap in the studied pipelines: fixed-distribution judging accuracy does not determine downstream optimization quality. The comparison changes judge-training objective as well as response format, and the main ranking is conditional on its learned reference rather than a universal human-quality result. A limited follow-up using a different learned judge is inconclusive overall.

classification.tldr: 研究生成式奖励模型的规模规律，发现静态判别准确率与在线策略优化效果存在评估者-奖励者差距，奖励模型容量对下游优化质量至关重要。

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Generative Reward Models

papers.abstractEn: Recent work established that the infinite-width and infinite-depth limits of residual networks commute at initialization when residual branches are scaled by $1/\sqrt{depth}$. In particular, the network output converges to the same limit whether width and depth tend to infinity sequentially or jointly. We extend this commutativity result to training in linear residual networks. Under the same $1/\sqrt{depth}$ residual-branch scaling (Depth-$μ$P) and the $μ$P width parameterization, we prove that, for any fixed number of gradient-descent steps with gradient clipping, the network output converges in $L^2$ along every joint width--depth growth path as both width and depth tend to infinity. Consequently, the infinite-width and infinite-depth limits commute throughout any finite training horizon. Without gradient clipping, the corresponding $L^2$ convergence does not hold in general, but we establish the weaker convergence in probability.

classification.tldr: 在线性残差网络中证明在Depth-μP参数化下，无限宽与无限深极限在整个有限训练过程中可交换，并给出梯度裁剪条件下的L2收敛保证。

papers.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute During Training

papers.abstractEn: Safety probes trained on a model's activations are a standard tool for monitoring language models in real time. Each time a new model is released or a new harm area needs to be monitored, the probe must be retrained, which requires new labels and a choice of probe architecture. Yet neither the model nor the labels tell us in advance how well the resulting probe will perform. Finding out requires training and comparing many probe configurations. In this paper, we ask whether probe performance can instead be predicted in advance from model size and the number of labels. Existing safety datasets are insufficient for this, as they are either limited in scale or already saturated. We therefore construct six new safety datasets of sufficient size and difficulty. On these datasets, we train two probe architectures on 20 base models from five model families, with 32 to $10^{6}$ labels for each model. We measure performance using probe error, defined as 1 - AUROC, where lower values are better. We find that probe error follows two simple scaling laws. First, the lowest probe error a model can reach falls as a power law in its size. Second, probe error decreases towards its floor as the number of examples increases; the slope increases as the target model size increases. Both laws hold across tasks, model families and probe architectures, and only their fitted constants differ. When fitted on the smallest models of a family, the laws predict the error of the next larger model to within 0.02 in 72% of cases. They also identify whether more labels or a larger model is the cheaper way to reach a target error in 73% of cases. Finally, they choose the probe architecture with an extra error of only 0.006 on average when they pick the worse one. These laws allow safety researchers to determine how to create the best probe for any given model and label budget.

classification.tldr: 构建六个安全数据集并训练大量探针，发现安全探针误差随模型规模和标注量呈幂律缩放，可提前预测探针性能并指导资源分配。

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes

papers.abstractEn: Which pretraining objective yields the best representation for downstream tasks under an information budget? We formalize this problem as a multitask information bottleneck, using a mutual information constraint to model incomplete information retention. For Gaussian inputs and tasks, we characterize optimal representations and show that a weakly task-aligned specialist can outperform a reconstruction generalist at low rates but lose at high rates. We also construct task families for which every fixed Gaussian prediction objective incurs arbitrarily large relative regret, driven by reversals in optimal allocation priorities. Conversely, the average task information matrix defines an objective with a uniform relative-regret bound controlled by maximum task SNR. CelebA and dSprites experiments illustrate that compression can change which pretraining objective performs best, and even task-aware training can reverse which downstream task is better preserved as rate increases.

classification.tldr: 以信息瓶颈形式化分析不同预训练目标在信息预算约束下的最优表示，发现任务对齐的专用目标在低码率下可胜过通用重建目标，但最优选择会随码率反转。

papers.title: Optimal Multitask Representations Under a Rate Constraint: An Information Bottleneck Analysis

papers.abstractEn: Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. We study PolarGD, the orthogonalized update at the core of Muon, on matrix quadratics, where optimizers can be analyzed in closed form, and compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. PolarGD reaches the minimizer in one step whenever the rows of the error are orthogonal with equal norms, for any Hessian, whereas gradient descent needs all Hessian eigenvalues to be equal; and unlike sign descent, PolarGD is unaffected by rotations of the problem. Over many steps, PolarGD acts as gradient descent preconditioned by the current iterate, so its speed is governed by the conditioning of the iterate rather than of the Hessian. This explains fast regimes as well as a slow one, caused by tiny singular values of the iterate, in which PolarGD is much slower than gradient descent. Finally, the few Newton-Schulz iterations used in Muon treat these tiny singular values as gradient descent does, so fewer iterations can converge faster than exact orthogonalization; in a transformer trained with Muon, about a quarter of the singular values of the attention matrices fall in this regime.

classification.tldr: 在二次矩阵问题上对Muon的正交化更新进行闭式分析，刻画其何时优于梯度下降、揭示慢收敛区域，并解释Newton-Schulz少量迭代反而可能更有利。

papers.title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz

papers.abstractEn: Training generative models on synthetic data causes loss of diversity and a decrease in performance, a phenomenon known as model collapse. We study this degeneration spectrally in a controlled Markov setting. The eigenvalue spectrum of the learned transition operator offers a direct view of the process, since the subdominant eigenvalues set how fast the chain mixes and therefore how much of the state space it continues to explore. We find that sampling at temperature $T_s < 1$ acts on the operator like repeated sharpening, pushing it toward a deterministic system: the subdominant eigenvalues approach the unit circle and the spectral gap narrows. When $T_s < 1$, even data accumulation does not appear to arrest this drift. We then analyze Dreaming Learning, a regulariser that, in parallel with regular training, adds a loss term on the model's own samples drawn at a raised temperature $T_d > 1$. Because high-temperature samples flatten the predicted distribution, training on them keeps the entries of the learned operator from becoming vanishingly small, which in turn keeps the eigenvalues bounded away from the unit circle. Measurements of the spectra over 5000 generations are consistent with this picture, and the mitigation effect persists in more complex settings such as LSTM language models and a 124M-parameter GPT-2.

classification.tldr: 从转移算子谱的角度分析合成数据训练导致的模型坍缩机理，并提出在高温自采样上附加损失的正则化方法以维持谱隙、缓解多样性退化。

papers.title: Mitigating Model Collapse through Dreaming Learning

papers.abstractEn: We study gradient flow in a two-layer linear network in the high-dimensional regime where the input, inner and output dimensions diverge proportionally. Under whitened inputs and isotropic imbalance, we combine a closed-form solution of the dynamics with prior random matrix theory results to derive a high-dimensional limit for the dynamics. Our method yields exact asymptotic spectral distributions for the weight matrices at all times and characterizes the evolution of the learned subspace. In the small-initialization limit, we identify a silent alignment phenomenon: the singular directions of the network align on an order-one timescale, while the singular values and empirical loss remain at their initial values. Visible learning occurs later, on a logarithmic timescale, as singular values progressively escape zero and the loss decreases. This phase is characterized by a saddle-to-saddle dynamics, which becomes a continuous process of spectral learning in the high-dimensional limit.

classification.tldr: 在高维极限下精确求解两层线性网络的梯度流动动力学，发现小初始化时奇异方向先在对数时间尺度前静默对齐而损失不变，随后奇异值逃逸零点进入可见学习阶段，呈现鞍点到鞍点动力学。

papers.title: Silent Alignment in Two-Layer Linear Networks: A High-Dimensional Perspective

papers.abstractEn: Pixel language models process text as rendered images instead of a finite vocabulary, which gives them strong cross-lingual transfer abilities. However, not much is known about how these abilities are influenced by larger-scale pretraining. In this paper, we train a family of MPIXEL models along three axes of variation: more languages, more scripts, and larger model capacity under fixed per-language compute. In evaluations on five tasks covering 83 languages, we find that scaling acts locally: each axis improves the added languages and scripts, while increased capacity mitigates the curse of multilinguality from pretraining on more languages. Transfer to unseen scripts improves with multilingual pretraining, but does not further improve with scaling. On typologically distant low-resource languages, our models outperform subword and character-level baselines across many writing systems. We also show that larger pixel models reserve more layers for visual processing, and that cross-lingual alignment weakens as more languages are added. Overall, our findings characterize how multilingual scaling improves pixel language models.

classification.tldr: 通过沿语言、文字和模型容量三个轴系统扩展像素语言模型的预训练，揭示多语言扩展对各能力的局部化影响规律。

papers.title: Scaling Multilingual Pretraining of Pixel Language Models

papers.abstractEn: We study an extremal regression problem, an example of multiple instance learning (MIL), where the predictors are given as multisets, called bags. The bag elements (called instances) possess hidden labels which are pooled to produce an observed bag-level label. Max pooling is common in MIL applications, but gives rise to vanishing gradients. To handle this, modern MIL pipelines approximate the max with a softmax, treating the sharpness as a learnable parameter, denoted $λ$. When the max pooling model is the true data generating process, learning will be successful when $λ$ is increased during gradient descent, thereby driving the dynamics into regions of parameter space with vanishing gradients. To understand the conditions under which gradient descent breaks down, we study a minimal model and derive a low dimensional projection of the gradient flow in the joint limit of large bags $n$ and high dimension $d$ with $α=\ln n/d$ fixed. The flow has two distinct phase transitions: an intrinsic freezing transition related to the random energy model of disordered systems, and a retrieval transition occurring in modern Hopfield networks. Numerical simulation confirms both the phase diagram and the convergence of the finite-size training gradient to its predicted asymptotic form.

classification.tldr: 研究基于极大值池化的多示例学习中的梯度流动力学，在大规模极限下推导出低维投影并发现冻结相变与检索相变两个相变，数值模拟验证了相图预测。

papers.title: Phase Transitions in Learning Driven by Extremal Data

papers.abstractEn: We are the first to give a certified rule for whether unseen data belong in a pretrained model's context or its weights, built on an exact law for their information value. That value, the code length saved on held-out queries, equals in expectation the bits stored about the query, plus a prior repair, minus a decoding loss, for any model, architecture, dataset and task. The law's ceilings certify the choice from one measurement, and an anytime-valid test makes it from held-out queries, with error controlled whenever it stops. Every certificate the ceilings issue on a trained transformer, TabPFN, an occupancy network and a stereo network is correct. The test picks TabPFN over XGBoost and a trained surrogate over an in-context learner on airfoil pressure, calls the better of GPT-2's cache and fine-tune in 61,948 of 64,000 query streams over 32 comparisons, and errs in at most 3.3% of null streams. The law also diagnoses when learning in context helps and when it does not. Deleting part of a context is held-out validation of that part in any model, and adding parts one at a time traces the learning curve in context: one patch that sees a shape feature cuts an occupancy network's code length there a hundredfold, while eight that miss it nearly double it, and one camera that sees the surface beats four in a stereo network. Ranked by this label-free valuation, a kriging learner's three best support cars beat four drawn at random, and on a yes-or-no claim the valuation recovers a published evidence adjudicator, with AUROC 0.91.

classification.tldr: 提出一个信息论定律与认证规则，判断新数据应放入预训练模型的上下文还是权重，并通过随时有效的检验在多个模型和任务上做出正确选择。

papers.title: When Thoughts Become Memory: Unifying In-Context Learning and Fine-Tuning

papers.abstractEn: Long-context continual pre-training (LCCP) is widely used to improve long-context capability, but how its benefits scale with the number of tokens used for LCCP remains unclear. We investigate this question through modeling, monitoring, and validating the benefits of scaling LCCP. First, we establish an empirical additive power law relating long-context performance to model size and the respective token budgets of short-context pre-training and LCCP. Experiments across five model scales and more than one hundred short- and long-context budget configurations show that the fitted law reproduces the observed trends and extrapolates well to held-out model scales. Second, we introduce \textsc{Constant-Last4}, a training and observation protocol that averages the four most recent consecutive checkpoints from a constant-learning-rate run to enable stable monitoring along a single extensible training trajectory. Under this protocol, the same scaling-law form fits well and accurately predicts the LCCP performance trajectory of a 1.22B-parameter model trained on approximately 100B LCCP tokens. Finally, downstream evaluations along this trajectory show continued improvements in long-context performance, with no clear sign of saturation within the evaluated range. These gains persist after both 128K context extension and supervised fine-tuning, with benefits extending to long-context understanding and agentic tasks. Together, these results argue for continuing to scale LCCP rather than stopping early: its gains are stably observable along an extensible trajectory, quantitatively predictable, and transferable to downstream tasks.

classification.tldr: 该研究通过跨五个模型规模的实验建立长上下文持续预训练收益的经验幂律，并提出稳定的训练观测协议，证明持续扩展LCCP可获得可预测且不饱和的长上下文能力提升。

papers.title: Don't Stop Long-Context Continual Pre-Training Too Early: An Empirical Scaling Law

papers.abstractEn: Mid-training (MT) is a training phase in LLM training pipelines that continues pretraining (PT) on smaller datasets of higher value. Taking the PT and MT phases as a whole, training usually starts with only PT data and then transitions completely to MT data. In this work, we view this complete transition from PT to MT data as a special case of a broader class of data mixing schedules that specify how the proportions of PT and MT tokens in each batch change over training. Under fixed total training compute and MT token budgets, we ask: Is this complete transition to MT data optimal for minimizing final MT loss? We show that the answer depends on the learning rate (LR) schedule: one data schedule may outperform another under one LR schedule, but changing only the LR schedule can reverse the outcome. Specifically, when the LR decays throughout continued training, introducing MT data earlier and mixing it with PT data lowers the final MT loss compared with placing all MT data at the end of training, but this result is reversed if we use constant LR. We therefore study how to jointly choose when to introduce MT data and when to decay the LR through ablation studies, and find that it is better to decay the LR only after MT data enters training. Finally, we develop a theoretical model that explains why the optimal data schedule for a fixed MT token budget depends on the LR schedule.

classification.tldr: 研究预训练与中期训练数据配比调度和学习率调度的联合设计，发现最优数据引入时机依赖于学习率衰减策略并给出理论解释。

papers.title: Data Schedules and Learning Rate Schedules Should Be Designed Together

papers.abstractEn: Why large language models trained via log-loss minimization over massive and diverse datasets exhibit broad capabilities and generalizable skills is not yet fully understood. Grau-Moya et al. (ICML 2024) offer a conceptual explanation through the lens of meta-learning: if sequence-generating environments $ν$ are drawn from a prior $w_ν$, minimizing population log-loss recovers the corresponding Bayesian mixture predictor $ξ=\sum_νw_νν$. In the idealized limit in which $w$ is a universal prior, the optimal predictor corresponds to Solomonoff universal induction. Practical machine learning algorithms, however, generally produce only \emph{approximately} optimal predictors. This raises a natural question: \emph{Does the prediction performance remain robust under approximation}? In this paper, we first provide a tight bound on the worst-case effect of approximation on prediction error. We show any predictor $ρ$ satisfying $D_{KL}(ξ\|ρ)\leq η$ retains bounded cumulative-expected-squared prediction error. However, while the Bayesian mixture predictor $ξ$ has error $O(\log(1/w_μ))$ in an environment $μ$, we establish a tight $Θ(η/w_μ)$ bound on the excess error of $ρ$ relative to $ξ$. Thus, approximation can substantially degrade performance in environments assigned small prior probability. In sharp contrast, when environments are averaged according to prior $w$, we prove that the excess prediction error is only $O(η)$. Furthermore, we establish a distribution-shift theorem for dominated shifts from a training prior $w$ to a test prior $w'$, interpolating our average-case and worst-case guarantees. Finally, we extend our robustness analysis to a finite-sampling setting relevant to learning universal predictors with neural networks and Transformers, where $D_{KL}(ξ\|ρ)$ could be unbounded. [For the full abstract, see the paper.]

classification.tldr: 从近似所罗门诺夫归纳的角度给出理论界，刻画以对数损失训练的通用预测器在近似误差和分布偏移下预测性能的鲁棒性条件。

papers.title: Approximate Solomonoff Induction: On the Robustness of Learned Universal Predictors

papers.abstractEn: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

classification.tldr: 论文证明可定义势函数的梯度轨迹具有有限球面长度并方向收敛，并据此推出深度网络训练流在可定义激活与损失下必然方向收敛。

papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials

papers.abstractEn: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) has established itself as a widely used method for training deep neural networks. Despite its popularity, existing convergence guarantees for SAM-type methods require smoothness, a restrictive assumption. Generalized smoothness conditions have recently been proposed in the analysis of gradient methods but remain underexplored for SAM. To analyze the effect of SAM's perturbation under generalized smoothness, we use relative gradient distortion to quantify how the sharpness-aware direction departs from the original gradient. Under $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness, we show that this distortion can become unbounded near stationarity for SAM and at large gradients for its unnormalized variant (USAM), with examples where SAM cycles and USAM diverges. We then establish a necessary condition for uniform distortion control among perturbations along the gradient whose nonnegative multipliers depend only on its norm. Motivated by this condition, we propose Curvature-Scaled SAM (CS-SAM), which scales both the perturbation and the descent step by suitable curvature upper bounds, and prove that it uniformly bounds the distortion. Under both $(L_0,L_1)$- and $(H_0,H_1)$-smoothness, we establish deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the best squared gradient norm on nonconvex objectives, last-iterate $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the function gap on convex objectives with a minimizer, and linear convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. With zero perturbation, our guarantees recover the rates for gradient descent with $(L_0,L_1)$- or $(H_0,H_1)$-based step-sizes. Minibatch experiments on computer vision tasks demonstrate competitive performance for both variants, with the $(H_0,H_1)$ variant achieving the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four settings against tuned SAM and USAM with constant and cosine annealing schedules.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出曲率缩放的SAM优化方法CS-SAM，在广义光滑条件下统一控制梯度畸变，并给出非凸、凸和PL条件下的收敛率保证。

papers.title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness

papers.abstractEn: Dropout and zoneout are routinely added to long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks, but, to our knowledge, their placements have not been crossed with gate initialisation in a factorial design, and it is not known whether early gradient propagation tells which runs will learn long dependencies. We trained one-layer LSTMs and GRUs on the adding problem and on delayed recall in a factorial grid of 720 runs, crossing conventional and chrono gate initialisation with up to six recurrent regulariser placements at one rate each, with pre-specified follow-ups, and recorded how sensitive the final hidden state was to the input at every lag. Because both tasks supply fresh or exhaustive training data, the study measures the regularisers' effects on optimisation and does not assess generalisation from a finite training set. At lengths chosen to make conventional initialisation difficult, all 360 chrono-initialised runs reached the validation criterion within 5000 updates, as did 119 of 120 unregularised runs with a horizon about four times too short or too long, whereas conventionally initialised networks learned slowly or did not reach the criterion within the budget at the longer lengths. Under conventional initialisation, dropout generally delayed learning and zoneout helped only in some conditions. The early input sensitivity added little to predicting which conditions learn once the early validation loss was modelled per task, architecture and initialisation. Within conditions, a flatter early decay went with the seeds that learned, but in a pre-specified test the association was modest (concordance 0.61), condition-dependent and not robust to resampling seeds. The results support chrono initialisation, even with a rough horizon, on such tasks.

classification.tldr: 通过720组因子化实验系统比较LSTM与GRU中门控初始化、循环dropout和zoneout对长依赖学习的影响，发现chrono初始化在困难长度下显著更优。

papers.title: Gate Initialisation versus Recurrent Dropout and Zoneout in Learning Long Dependencies: A Controlled Study of LSTM and GRU Networks on Synthetic Tasks

papers.abstractEn: Muon orthogonalizes a weight matrix's momentum before each step, and on neural networks this simple preconditioner beats AdamW in a wide range of tasks. Existing analyses explain Muon within general optimization frameworks or on a few specific models, and many of them view orthogonalization as a preconditioner. Since the Hessian is the optimal preconditioner under a quadratic approximation of the loss, these works leave a basic question open: what makes orthogonalization suited to the Hessian of a neural network? Prior work shows that the layer-wise Hessian of a neural network is row-block diagonally dominant, and Muon's implicit preconditioner, the Kronecker product $(\mathbf{V}\mathbf{V}^\top)^{1/2}\otimes\mathbf{I}$ with $\mathbf{V}$ the momentum, has the same row-block structure exactly when $\mathbf{V}\mathbf{V}^\top$ is diagonally dominant. Diagonal dominance of $\mathbf{V}\mathbf{V}^\top$ has been observed in language models, but why a neural network produces it has not been explained. This work provides a quantitative asymptotic theory for neural networks at initialization, and points out the intuition that the overparameterization of the weight matrices drives the diagonal dominance. We analyze $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{G}\mathbf{G}^\top]$, which equals $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{V}\mathbf{V}^\top]$ at initialization, in four canonical models: symmetric matrix factorization, deep linear networks, two-layer ReLU networks, and single-layer linear attention. In each case the diagonal entries outgrow the off-diagonal ones at explicit rates as the hidden dimensions grow; for the query, key and value weights of attention the off-diagonal vanishes altogether. Simulations of the four models and experiments on language models at initialization confirm the predicted scaling.

classification.tldr: 该文给出初始化时的渐近理论，解释过参数化如何导致梯度自外积的对角占优，从而说明Muon正交化预条件子为何适配神经网络的Hessian结构。

papers.title: How Does Orthogonalization Adapt to the Neural Network Hessian Structure? A Gradient Self Outer-Product Analysis at Initialization

papers.abstractEn: Looped transformers reuse one block of layers many times and are often trained by backpropagating through only the last k loops. We measure how much of the weight gradient this throws away, exactly and for every k from one backward pass, on nine looped language models, and report three findings.
