First, on a trained model this lost gradient is set near the output: once the loop count is well above k, it barely changes with the loop count (within about 0.03 from 32 to 64 loops on the three models we tested, as a pre-registered test predicted for Parcae). Where the backward signal shrinks, $ρ^k$, with $ρ$ the signal's fitted shrink per loop, approximates it at moderate loop counts but overstates it at long ones, because the fitted $ρ$ drifts up as the fit takes in more loops. On Ouro the signal grows, and keeping two of four loops still loses 81% of the final output's gradient. Second, the lost gradient falls during fine-tuning, by 0.07-0.22 within 300 steps on three of four models, on held-out problems too. The fall is not just the read-out's share of the gradient; training only the layers outside the loop reproduced up to half of it, and it also falls under truncated training. So a trained model's value overstates what truncation removes later. Third, we could not show that it predicts the training cost of truncation better than rules that need no measurement: on two new models it tied Parcae's cost at the same k, in a test too small to separate them.

classification.tldr: 精确测量循环Transformer截断反向传播丢失的梯度，发现训练后丢失梯度集中于输出层且随微调下降，为截断训练提供实证依据。

papers.title: How Much Gradient Does Truncated Backprop Lose in Looped Transformers?

papers.abstractEn: A systematic understanding of the global structure of neural-network loss landscapes remains challenging due to their high dimensionality. Symmetries arising from network architectures and learning objectives provide a way to investigate aspects of this structure. Although a growing number of studies have drawn attention to these symmetries, a systematic characterization of them, as well as of the critical orbits they give rise to, remains incomplete. To address this gap, in this work we establish a topological symmetry index, based on the methodologies from the family of equivariant degree theories, to decode these symmetries. The frameworks apply to arbitrary network architectures and include methods applicable to degenerate critical orbits. The index detects the isotropy of the critical points and quantifies the corresponding net topological contributions. Several examples, including softplus MLPs, Transformers, and equivariant neural networks, are presented to illustrate the computations.

classification.tldr: 基于等变度理论构造拓扑对称性指标，系统刻画神经网络损失景观中对称性导致的临界轨道，并适用于多种网络架构。

papers.title: A General Topological Symmetry Index for Critical Orbits In Neural Network Loss Landscapes

papers.abstractEn: Latent diffusion models almost universally place a Gaussian prior on the VAE latent space. For base generation this default is unproblematic; under reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, however, it carries a structural limitation. The standard VAE's KL term does not merely ignore mode structure - it actively taxes separation and tightness. When data are multimodal, the ELBO optimum compresses distinct modes into an overlapping latent. RL fine-tuning amplifies this overlap: the score network is under-resolved on the saddle region between modes, dynamic-to-variational amplification rises sharply, and the collapse boundary beta_c is pushed far above its variational scale. On the real alanine-dipeptide Boltzmann distribution, a Gaussian-prior VAE collapses at beta_c = 0.224 while a mode-tracked Gaussian-mixture prior collapses at 0.00316, a 71x gap from the same pipeline. We trace this gap to a single geometric mediator, d_min/(2 sigma_0), and verify the causal chain through controlled interventions: moving geometry at fixed prior, and switching prior at matched geometry (full mediation; prior-label coefficient 0.995x, 95% CI [0.79, 1.25]). A three-source decomposition localises the amplification to the learned policy (zero ODE-solver contribution, bounded anchor mismatch); the coverage plateau is an unconditional benefit of mode-separating priors that no amount of RL capacity recovers. The remedy is conditional: a non-Gaussian prior is necessary precisely when the latent geometry would fall into overlap and the task is coverage-sensitive. A machine-checked theory skeleton supports the KL pricing structure - a divergent compactness tax under a Gaussian prior versus a finite assignment fee under a mixture - and the position-versus-plateau distinction delimits what is finite-resource from what requires changing the prior.

classification.tldr: 该理论研究扩散模型RL微调中高斯先验失效的几何机制，证明了模态重叠导致坍缩，并提出混合先验可大幅提升覆盖能力。

papers.title: When Do Gaussian Priors Fail? A Latent Geometry Investigation of RL Fine-Tuning

papers.abstractEn: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is the cornerstone of modern deep learning, yet its theoretical convergence properties remain poorly understood in non-convex settings. To address this gap, we study SGD dynamics in deep linear neural networks - simplified models that retain key non-convex characteristics while remaining analytically tractable. Building on recent results for gradient descent, we extend convergence guarantees to SGD under regularized squared loss. We establish almost sure boundedness of SGD iterates. Using the framework of asymptotic pseudotrajectories from stochastic approximation theory, our analysis establishes then, for both deterministic and adaptive step-size choices, convergence of SGD to the set of critical points under mild conditions (without relying on Lipschitz properties or whitened data). To our knowledge, this is the first work providing almost sure convergence guarantees for SGD in deep linear networks, bridging the gap between theoretical optimization and practical stochastic training.

classification.tldr: 在深度线性神经网络中首次建立SGD几乎必然收敛到临界点的理论保证，适用于确定性与自适应步长，且无需Lipschitz条件或白化数据。

papers.title: Convergence of stochastic gradient descent for learning linear neural networks

papers.abstractEn: A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.

classification.tldr: 从神经模型几何角度分析局部极小值是否落在含失活神经元的子模型中，证明除少数例外子模型偏好无法由几何解释，须归因于训练动力学等因素。

papers.title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?

papers.abstractEn: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves data efficiency but generalizes worse to distant worlds under single-world training; (2) we observe an early interface phase with broad cross-world benefits and a later world phase with gains narrowed to in-corpus and related worlds, and fit an empirical scaling law relating validation loss to data volume, diversity and model size; and (3) our models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings. However, the limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training.

classification.tldr: 通过120组继续预训练配置系统研究数据量、多样性与模型规模对虚拟世界具身智能体的影响，拟合出经验缩放律并揭示模仿学习在远域泛化上的局限。

papers.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds

papers.abstractEn: Polyak--Ruppert averaging gives SGD and momentum methods the same asymptotic covariance. We characterize how fast finite runs reach it and how far they can be parallelized. For strongly convex quadratics with additive noise, we prove an online--offline bridge: the empirical risk minimizer on the samples of a tail average is one Newton step from the tail-averaged query point of any online procedure. For SGD, heavy ball, and Nesterov's method with constant momentum, this step is a boundary term at the two ends of the tail and splits the gap to the offline estimator into center, covariance, and shape errors. Necessary and sufficient conditions show that, on the least curved direction, the center error sets the pace: SGD needs $m\ggκ^2$ rounds but momentum only $m\ggκ$, where $κ$ is the condition number, so at sample size $N$ the critical batch size grows from $Θ(\sqrt{N}/κ)$ to $Θ(\sqrt{N/κ})$. The covariance error separates the momentum methods: heavy ball has relative variance excess $Θ(κ^{3/2}/m)$ along the stiffest direction, whereas Nesterov has relative error $O(\sqrtκ/m)$ in every direction. The shape error is method-independent by a Berry--Esseen bound uniform in $κ$ and batch size, so confidence intervals are valid when the other two errors vanish. We further examine how the conclusions change under heavy-tailed or state-dependent noise and clipping, and establish a first-order comparison with ERM for nonlinear Nesterov averaging under explicit conditions.

classification.tldr: 理论刻画动量法下Polyak-Ruppert平均的收敛速率，证明动量可将条件数依赖从κ²降至κ并比较各方法方差。

papers.title: When Momentum Helps Polyak--Ruppert Averaging

papers.abstractEn: In earlier work by Jonasson, Steif and Zetterqvist (2023), fully connected deep neural networks with layers of width $n$, i.i.d.\ standard Gaussian weights, sign activations and no bias terms were shown to be annealed and quenched noise sensitive with respect to any joint probability distribution $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}$ on the input $\boldsymbolω$ and its perturbation $\boldsymbolη$ satisfying a mild positive-correlation condition and $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbolη \in \{\boldsymbolω,-\boldsymbolω\}) \to 0$. Here we add independent Gaussian biases of the natural order and show that quenched noise sensitivity is retained over a broad range of depths, indeed under the slightly weaker assumption that $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbolω = \boldsymbolη) \to 0$. Thus, subject to the positive-correlation condition, quenched noise sensitivity holds under the minimal requirement that the perturbed input is asymptotically unlikely to coincide with the original input. At the same time, the annealed covariance remains bounded away from zero and is entirely accounted for by fluctuations in the network-dependent output means.

classification.tldr: 从理论上证明带高斯偏置的符号激活深度网络在温和条件下仍保持淬火噪声敏感性，同时退火协方差有下界。

papers.title: Annealed correlation and quenched noise sensitivity in biased deep neural networks

papers.abstractEn: Direct preference optimisation (DPO) is widely used for language model post-training, but its performance depends strongly on the choice of its hyperparameters, such as the learning rate and the reference-policy regularisation parameter $β$. To better understand the DPO hyperparameter landscape, we conduct extensive experiments using a dense hyperparameter grid across different model scales from the same family. This allows us to analyse how the optimal DPO hyperparameters evolve with model size and the number of update steps, with intermediate checkpoints providing an inexpensive signal to accelerate the hyperparameter optimisation process. Furthermore, by evaluating our models on both static and dynamic benchmarks, we identify which benchmarks provide the strongest signal for hyperparameter selection. Finally, we investigate how different state-of-the-art hyperparameter optimisation strategies perform in this setting. Our experiments show that the optimal learning rate varies with model size and that hyperparameters are not transferable across training datasets. We also find that validation loss is a poor proxy for hyperparameter optimisation, as hyperparameters that minimize validation loss only weakly correlate with optimal hyperparameters for downstream benchmarks. Therefore, DPO hyperparameters need to be tuned specifically for the target model, dataset, and evaluation objective. We also show that short candidate training runs can substantially reduce the cost of this selection. We release all our training configurations and evaluation results to support reproducible analysis of selection quality and training cost.

classification.tldr: 通过大规模网格实验刻画DPO超参数随模型规模和数据集的变化规律，证明超参数不可跨设置迁移且验证损失不是可靠的选参代理。

papers.title: The Shape of the DPO Hyperparameter Landscape: What to Measure, How It Moves with Scale, and When Not to Transfer It

papers.abstractEn: Empirical scaling laws relate validation loss to model size, training exposure and compute, providing a quantitative basis for allocating resources. This technical note explains these relationships through three linked analyses. Geometric approximation connects spatial resolution, intrinsic dimension and smoothness to function error; the loss function determines how that error transfers to task risk. Spectral analysis combines feature visibility, covariance eigenvalues and target alignment to describe how additional data reduce unresolved predictive mass. Constrained optimization then gives the parameter-data balance and the training-inference trade-off. We also examine emergence and grokking, separating scoring thresholds from learning dynamics, and test-time scaling, separating candidate coverage from selected-answer accuracy. Applications to vision and molecular prediction show how domain-specific coordinates change the resource comparison. An $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ case study quantifies the dimension dependence of quotient-space approximation gains and compares optimized compute frontiers, alongside separate analyses of conformational coverage and correlated-sample precision.

classification.tldr: 从几何逼近、谱分析和约束优化三方面为经验缩放律提供理论基础，并解释涌现、grokking与测试时扩展现象。

papers.title: Foundations of the Scaling Law

papers.abstractEn: Muon and related optimizers update a weight matrix with a spectrally transformed gradient. In this work, we study such spectral optimizers with a constant step size on strongly convex matrix quadratics, which isolate the effect of the update from the confounds of nonconvexity, noise, and step size schedules. We analyze an update using two quantities: the gain, which is the factor by which it amplifies the gradient along each singular direction, and the length, which is the norm of the update. These two quantities place the popular spectral updates in three regimes with different behavior: (i) with a bounded gain, the iterates behave like preconditioned gradient descent and converge for step sizes set by the largest curvature; (ii) with an unbounded gain but a vanishing length, they still converge, with the admissible step sizes set by the total curvature instead; and (iii) with a non-vanishing length, they do not converge for almost every initialization. Interestingly, the practical variants of Muon fall in all three regimes, depending only on how the update is normalized and scaled and not on the polynomial that approximates the polar factor. Experiments validate these findings.

classification.tldr: 理论上分析Muon类谱变换优化器在强凸二次问题上的恒定步长行为，按增益与长度刻画三种收敛机制并给出步长条件。

papers.title: Constant Step Sizes for Muon-Type Spectral Optimizers on Strongly Convex Quadratics

papers.abstractEn: When unique pretraining data is scarce, models see the same tokens many times and are thought to memorize. Random-token replacement, an input-corruption augmentation, is one remedy reported to lower validation loss, but a lower loss alone does not reveal which source of error it reduces. On a controlled source whose entropy rate is known in closed form, we show that replacement shrinks predictions toward the corpus average. We also introduce a decomposition that separates validation loss into approximation, estimation, and memorization terms. This shrinkage view predicts that replacement's bias cost needs no memorization but its benefit does. Memorization raises validation loss after its minimum, so we report the effect at two points, the minimum validation loss and the end of a fixed budget. Where replacement helps, it reduces this rise by about 60%. At the end of the budget, it turns from harmful to helpful as the controlled source becomes less predictable; at the minimum, it helps at no predictability level under the fixed recipe. On Korean and Japanese web text, replacement removes about a third of the loss rise after the minimum by the end of the budget, but its effect at the minimum is much smaller. Across ten real corpora, replacement lowers the final loss on nine. It harms only the census corpus, program-generated JSON that is the most redundant of the ten and much more redundant than any of 64 further prose and code corpora we measure.

classification.tldr: 提出基于已知熵的损失分解方法，将验证损失拆分为近似、估计与记忆项，理论结合十个真实语料实验揭示随机token替换在重复数据下降低记忆损失但引入偏差代价的规律。

papers.title: Benefit and Cost of Random-Token Replacement under Repeated Data: A Known-Entropy Decomposition and Evidence from Ten Real Corpora

papers.abstractEn: Low curvature trace, an effective rank condition, is a common explanation for why randomized zeroth-order methods scale to high-dimensional tasks such as language model fine-tuning. Can deterministic methods achieve the same savings? We show that they cannot. We study finding $\varepsilon$-stationary points of $L$-smooth nonconvex functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ from exact function values, assuming that below the starting value the Hessian is dominated by a fixed matrix with trace at most $LE$; this is the effective rank condition used to explain zeroth-order fine-tuning. When $ET\le d$, the Gaussian two-point method that such fine-tuning uses needs only $O(ET)$ calls if it rejects steps that raise $f$, where $T=LΔ/\varepsilon^2$ is the iteration count of gradient descent from initial gap $Δ$, and we prove that every randomized method needs $Ω(ET)$ calls, so this cost is optimal up to constants. In contrast, every deterministic method needs $\widetildeΩ(d\min\{T,\sqrt{ET}\})$ calls, and adaptive subspace search attains $O(d\min\{T,\sqrt{ET}\})$: a deterministic method pays about $d$ calls per discovered direction, and the trace budget allows about $\sqrt{ET}$ directions. Determinism thus multiplies the cost by a factor of order $d/(E+\sqrt{ET})$ up to logarithmic factors, which grows linearly with $d$ for fixed $E$ and $T$; once $E$ exceeds $T$ by a logarithmic factor, deterministic methods need $Ω(dT)$ calls, as without any trace budget. Our lower bounds hold for $C^\infty$ functions with the matrix bound on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, even when each call also returns gradient projections priced by rank.

classification.tldr: 证明在低曲率迹条件下确定性零阶优化方法相比随机方法存在随维度增长的固有调用次数下界，解释了随机化方法在高维微调中的必要性。

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Smooth Nonconvex Zeroth-Order Optimization: The Price of Determinism under Low Curvature Trace

papers.abstractEn: The represented gradient flow of a parameterized model depends on a mobility that can retain hidden parameter information. We study when one entire represented mobility map works for every autonomous loss from one fixed initialization. For two-factor matrix representations wider than both output dimensions, with individually full-row-rank factors, we classify all admissible joint ranks: closure occurs precisely at effective scalar-balanced minimal joint rank or a two-value signed spectral family at full joint rank. All intermediate ranks are excluded; positive represented flows belong to known square-root families. For general representations with constant ambient representation and gradient-Lie ranks, ordinary closure is equivalent to a local invariant-level metric in the analytic case and specified smooth regimes. An endpoint section forces the initially unrestricted mobility map to admit a locally smooth representative on the represented image. We also separate testing families: linear losses locally admit closure at every submersion, whereas one fixed translated strongly convex quadratic family fails it on a delayed-bracket example. A fixed output readout gives an ordinary squared-loss witness. These supporting results do not characterize quadratic-only closure in general. We retain the unresolved smooth output-rank-two case with Lie rank at least four. A frozen deterministic experiment checks a separate engineered-loss construction; it is distinguished from the squared-loss proof, universal theorems and empirical learning performance.

classification.tldr: 该文从理论上刻画参数化模型表示空间中梯度流的闭合条件，对两因子矩阵表示给出全部容许联合秩的精确分类，并证明一般表示下闭合等价于局部的不变层级度量。

papers.title: When Parameter Gradient Flows Close in Representation Space

papers.abstractEn: We analytically study the evolution of the energy function of Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) as they train on randomly sampled codewords of random expander low-density parity-check codes (a.k.a. solutions of random XORSAT problems). We identify two distinct regimes and a transition between them, reminiscent of grokking in neural networks. A regime of small training set size is where the model memorizes a few training examples but cannot discover the underlying rules of the entire codeword dictionary generative process. The opposite regime, corresponding to a larger training set size, is where the model has uncovered the sparse constraints that generated the entire data set after seeing only polynomially many patterns. We also design a novel class of DenseAMs with a thresholding learning rule, and show that any amount of thresholding enables the model to perform simplified sparse Hamiltonian learning, which exponentially reduces the number of training examples needed to learn the true underlying data set. In this regime, the model learns how to discover $\exp[\mathrm{O}(n)]$ solutions from only $\mathrm{O}(\log n)$ training samples, which is asymptotically optimal for any learning algorithm. When training on codewords of certain random codes, the model can even learn the underlying code when a small O(1) fraction of bits are latent variables. These latent variables are not shown to the model during learning, but will be discovered by sparsifying observed higher-order correlations. For certain random codes, we show that a simple and conservative algorithm learns a minimal latent representation for the data set. This provides a transparent, physics-motivated, and analytically tractable toy model for how deep latent representations emerge in an associative memory training.

classification.tldr: 该文通过解析研究稠密联想记忆的能量函数演化，刻画了类似grokking的相变，并提出阈值学习规则使样本需求指数级降低。

papers.title: Sample-efficient learning with Dense Associative Memories

papers.abstractEn: Gradient descent with momentum can be viewed as a particle moving with friction in the loss landscape. In deep learning the learning rate is usually large, so training is a discrete dynamical system: in many full-batch experiments the sharpness grows to the optimizer's stability limit, the edge of stability (EoS), and training continues there. Physics-inspired optimizers change this motion; Velocity-Regularized Adam (VRAdam), for example, shrinks the step at high speed. We study kinetic maps, in which the step is the gradient of a kinetic energy of the momentum, and ask what they do beyond the EoS. (i) In a reduced model, a kinetic map creates a symmetric period-two orbit beyond the edge, strictly linearly stable if and only if the map's elasticity (the log-log slope of step length versus momentum) lies between 0 and 1; on it, training sits at an effective edge of stability. VRAdam's damper fails above twice the critical learning rate, where its kinetic energy is not convex; the Legendre dual of VRAdam's own Lagrangian is convex and passes at every learning rate. (ii) Because the sharpness rises gradually, the loss of stability is delayed, as in Neishtadt's theory of slowly swept bifurcations. In a network with a controlled sweep, the dynamics match this theory without fitted parameters, including the memory of where the sweep started and its erasure by noise. (iii) With momentum, reaching the oscillation also requires elasticity at large momentum: maps that bound the step have competing period-four and chaotic attractors already at beta1 = 0.9, while the cubic-Legendre map reached the oscillation from every sampled start up to beta1 = 0.99. Experiments on an exact quadratic problem, a full-batch MLP and ResNet-32 support the theory; on ResNet-18, much of the apparent benefit of the maps is reproduced by matching the effective learning rate.

classification.tldr: 以动力系统理论分析物理启发优化器在稳定性边缘之外的行为，证明周期二轨道的稳定性条件并解释延迟失稳现象，实验与理论吻合。

papers.title: Physics-Inspired Optimizers beyond the Edge of Stability: Period-Two Orbits and Delayed Instability

papers.abstractEn: Over-fitted Gaussian mixtures can contain many parameter configurations with nearly the same density, making the order of density cancellation central to their parameter-learning rates. Ho and Nguyen encoded these cancellations in a polynomial system and conjectured its exact order as a function of cluster size. The key to resolving the conjecture is a common positive-variance shift that turns the coefficient equations into Gaussian moment matching. For every cluster size $\Mhn\ge2$, we prove that the real, nonzero-weight system has order $2\Mhn$: a sharp sign-change bound forces rigidity at that order, while positive Gauss--Hermite quadrature constructs a non-trivial solution through order $2\Mhn-1$. Population-density calculations at 110-digit working precision recover the predicted leading term for two to six components; finite multistart searches recover the same observed powers for two to five components, with smaller finite-scale constants for three to five components. For parameter learning, the exact order gives an explicit pointwise maximum-likelihood exponent and an exact local minimax order on specified shrinking neighbourhoods of a fixed known mixing measure. The same coefficient viewpoint separates high-order cancellation from exact parameter symmetries in mixtures of experts. Synchronized replication preserves the conditional density while keeping the corresponding parameter losses positive in two broad standard-softmax classes, showing why statistical rate arguments must account for exact parameter symmetries.

classification.tldr: 证明高斯混合多项式系统的消除阶为2倍簇数，解决Ho-Nguyen猜想，并据此给出极大似然率与混合专家参数对称性的分析。

papers.title: Solving the Ho--Nguyen Conjecture for Gaussian Mixtures: Applications to Mixtures of Experts

papers.abstractEn: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. The analysis of experimental results motivates the Physical Barrel Hypothesis: different capabilities may constrain different parts of improvement. The five-axis metrics also distinguish systems with close public benchmark averages and show that high scores need not come with early or efficient gains. We study observational scaling from two perspectives: predicting the relative performance of VLM agents from their public capabilities, and forecasting later progress from early physical feedback. Together, these analyses ask how quickly and how far an agent can improve. Moreover, we conduct workspace interventions and then analyze what improvement leaves behind. Removing history reduces late-round success, frozen workspaces remain useful on unseen layouts, and three cross-task cases achieve success earlier. The results suggest that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist.

classification.tldr: 该研究构建了物理递归自我改进的五轴评测基准，并提出物理木桶假说与观测性缩放规律，用于预测VLM智能体在操作任务上的改进速度与上限。

papers.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy

papers.abstractEn: Recent work in tabular machine learning has emphasized the importance of diverse and realistic evaluation settings. The niche of large-scale (1M+) data, however, remains under-explored. To study training-data scaling, we assemble eight real-world tabular datasets with up to around ten million training examples, retaining the natural distribution shifts of the tasks and using random-split evaluation as a control. We find that GBDTs and MLP-based models show broadly similar scaling trends, with gains from both additional training data and algorithmic improvements. Tabular foundation models show more varied scaling behavior, with recent versions benefiting more consistently from larger contexts even under distribution shift. However, scaling training data under distribution shift introduces new challenges: in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance mostly improve together at smaller scales but can diverge at larger scales. We examine this through MLP capacity sweeps and comparisons of the validation distributions used for tuning and early stopping in MLPs and GBDTs. We also compare common practices of using validation data, contrasting its use for model selection in MLP pipelines with using it for in-context fitting in tabular foundation model pipelines. Under stronger shifts, MLPs selected using validation representative of the evaluation conditions generally maintain or improve performance as training data grows. In contrast, including such examples in context improves foundation-model performance, but does not prevent deterioration with increasing training size in our experiments.

classification.tldr: 构建八个大规模表格数据集研究训练数据规模扩展规律，发现分布偏移下GBDT、MLP与表格基础模型的扩展行为差异，以及验证集使用方式对性能的影响。

papers.title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?

papers.abstractEn: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.

classification.tldr: 提出一阶与零阶随机优化算法，用于在真实标签与机器预测标签混合的数据集上训练模型，从线性回归到LLM微调验证了方法有效性。

papers.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization

papers.abstractEn: We show that gradient descent (GD) with step size $η$ can achieve $\varepsilon$ optimality gap on the multiclass logistic regression loss in a number of iterations $T$ that is independent of $\varepsilon$. To do so, the step size $η$ must be chosen large enough as a function of $\varepsilon$ (and properties of the linearly separable dataset), while $T$ is a constant that only depends on the data. The relevant properties of the data include the number of points and their margin (for $T$), and one additional quantity (for $η$) that turns out to be necessary in dimension $d \geq 3$. The proofs build on the known fact that, as $η\to \infty$, suitably rescaled GD becomes the perceptron algorithm, and the latter finds a perfect classifier in $T$ iterations. A similar claim was shown for two classes in dimension $d = 2$ using other proof techniques. This result adds to previous works that showed GD on the logistic regression loss can be accelerated by taking large step sizes. Those provoke a wild, oscillatory initial phase, followed by a stable phase. We provide results of this (qualitatively different) nature, too.

classification.tldr: 论文证明在多类逻辑回归上，选取足够大的学习率可使梯度下降在与目标精度无关的固定迭代步数内达到任意小的最优性间隙，其证明将大步长梯度下降的极限与感知机算法联系起来。

papers.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression

papers.abstractEn: Consolidating specialized foundation models into a unified generalist is a central goal of post-training. Two approaches are in common use: model merging, which is fast but treated as a heuristic, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, which matches distributions but demands heavy rollout compute and suffers from cross-task gradient conflict. We show that the two are one objective seen at different orders. Within a shared basin of homologous specialists, the multi-teacher on-policy distillation objective is, to second order, exactly the Fisher-merging objective. Its minimizer is therefore the Fisher merge, a classic model-merging method given by a closed-form combination of the specialists, so merging is optimal, to second order, as a closed-form stage of distillation. Building on this identification, we propose Residual-Governed Branch-and-Merge(RGBM), a two-phase consolidation procedure. Concretely, a full-parameter Fisher merge is intractable on foundation models, so Phase~1 restricts the merge to the task-vector subspace. Extending tangent-space analyses of merging, we show that the same coefficients that mix task vectors also mix implicit rewards, which lets a residual program on unlabelled prompts solve for them. The program minimizes the worst per-domain residual and reports its energy-normalized values as the domain residual spectrum. Phase~2 lets this spectrum govern what may be added: RGBM passivates domains with low normalized residuals, trains isolated branches only for domains above the spectral gap, and writes back the admitted updates with calibrated shrinkage. On two open-source consolidation suites, the Phase~1 merge alone matches or outperforms fully trained multi-teacher distillation, and RGBM improves on it further with zero extra joint-training steps, whereas every un-gated write-back, including continued joint distillation from the merge, falls below it.

classification.tldr: 该论文从Fisher几何视角证明多教师在线蒸馏在二阶意义上等价于Fisher模型合并，并提出两阶段合并-蒸馏流程，仅用合并阶段即可匹配完整蒸馏效果。

papers.title: A Fisher-Geometric View of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

papers.abstractEn: Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). To save training compute, BPTT is often truncated to the last few loops, although this may weaken the benefit of looping. To study this tradeoff systematically, we jointly vary model size, training tokens, and forward and backward loop counts across nearly 600 training runs and fit a unified scaling law that captures the effects of looping and truncation through effective parameters. Despite the training-compute savings of truncation, our fitted law favors full BPTT when forward and backward loop counts are jointly optimized. In matched-compute runs, full BPTT through fewer loops consistently outperforms truncated settings of the same compute. The law further shows that at fixed model size, the compute-optimal loop count and training-token budget both grow with compute. When model size is also free, the law identifies two fully trained loops as the best looped setting. Experimentally, this setting achieves lower loss than the compute-optimal non-looped model with about 27% fewer non-embedding parameters and only 8% more training compute.

classification.tldr: 通过近600次训练联合变化模型规模、token量与循环次数拟合并统一缩放律，系统刻画截断BPTT的权衡，发现全BPTT更优且两个训练循环为计算最优设定，参数量减少约27%。

papers.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation

papers.abstractEn: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) learns from pairwise preferences through a logistic objective whose score-difference parameterization follows the Bradley--Terry model. We study how failure of this modeling assumption limits DPO, distinguishing structural misspecification from limited model capacity and finite-sample estimation. Our main contribution is a characterization of structural approximation error through the triangle-curl of the preference log-odds, which vanishes exactly when preferences admit a Bradley--Terry representation. We upper bound the achievable excess logistic risk by a score-class approximation term and a triangle-curl term, and establish a lower bound proportional to triangle-curl under additional boundedness assumptions. For ReLU score models, including clipped models, we derive explicit approximation rates showing that increasing capacity can eliminate the score-approximation term while leaving the structural obstruction unchanged. We further establish finite-sample bounds for clipped empirical risk minimizers that separate network approximation, structural misspecification, and estimation error. We place these results within a surrogate-risk framework by identifying contextual preference accuracy (CPA) as a natural measure of agreement between preference judgments and changes in pairwise probability ratios relative to the reference policy. Standard logistic consistency and calibration results connect DPO's objective to this policy property and transfer our excess-risk upper bounds to CPA, without treating CPA as a complete measure of generated-response quality.

classification.tldr: 从统计学习理论角度刻画DPO在Bradley-Terry模型假设失效时的结构性近似误差，给出上下界与有限样本风险分解。

papers.title: Statistical Learning Theory for Direct Preference Optimization

papers.abstractEn: We study the gradient flow training dynamics of two-layer multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) on anisotropic Gaussian data. Even in this simple setting, solving the dynamics in full is notoriously difficult, so we try something different. We propose a "feature ODE" that might be intuitively expected to describe the learning dynamics of a shallow MLP. We find that MLPs trained to learn simple target functions (low-order Hermite polynomials and staircase functions) actually roughly follow the loss trajectories from this feature ODE. This agreement is a surprise because of the size of the simplification and the fact that it does not come from a rigorous chain of approximations. We discuss this surprise and speculate on its reasons and uses.

classification.tldr: 提出描述浅层MLP学习动力学的特征ODE，发现训练低阶Hermite与阶梯函数时实际损失轨迹大致遵循该简化方程，并探讨其原因与用途。

papers.title: A "feature ODE" describing the learning behavior of shallow MLPs on simple functions
